purpose: Backfill explicit modern source-governance fields for the five configured monitor source families, while decomposing the Colombia composite source so distinct rights regimes are not collapsed into one source identity.

rba.finding: Most RBA-owned website material is CC BY 4.0 subject to explicit exclusions and third-party material conditions. This clears curated RBA-owned factual metadata, but the general copyright notice is not treated as a standalone automation licence.

eurlex_reuse.finding: EUR-Lex states that its data may be reused free of charge subject to copyright conditions and documents machine routes including webservices, bulk downloads, Cellar REST and SPARQL access.

commission_reuse.finding: EU-owned European Commission website content is generally licensed CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise indicated.

colombia_open_data.finding: Colombia's Open Data Portal permits free use, redistribution, compilation, extraction, modification and commercial/non-commercial use of portal data with attribution and preservation of applicable metadata.

suin_terms.finding: SUIN requires correct, lawful and diligent use, source citation and preservation of rights notices, and prohibits uses that overload, damage or disable the portal. A broad automated-reuse permission is therefore not inferred for the operative legal-text HTML route.

set.governance_backfill_basis: RBA-owned FSR publication metadata is reuse-cleared under the general CC BY 4.0 notice; the official RSS transport remains a live pilot but no broader automation permission is inferred from copyright terms alone.
EUR-Lex reuse guidance expressly provides machine access routes including Cellar REST/SPARQL and the current CRA Cellar route is live-validated.
Primary automated CBAM legal monitoring uses documented EUR-Lex/Cellar machine routes; Commission CBAM HTML is an official non-primary cross-check under the Commission reuse policy.
